findings.reason: Confirmed as a prospective ownership/dependency defect, not an existing atlas cycle. On cbdcb4b, DY.6 requires DY.4; route 5 imports DY.6 and DY.4 but exports back to DY.6, while item 10 and the packet's moduli-PCF equidistribution need the downstream bifurcation and quasi-projective inputs. The packet also leaves McMullen as an input to Ingram. Remove the reverse endpoint export and move the moduli-PCF application downstream, but those edits alone do not close the dependency chain. Coordinate early critical-height definitions and early bifurcation/rigidity suppliers separately from late equidistribution and uniform endpoints, with explicit rescope/split requests and an acyclic dependency test. Keep generic Arakelov acceptance independent of critical-height applications. PCF and flexible-Lattes definitions are existing DY.6 plans (/5), not new Part II definitions. Do not declare that DY.6 imports nothing from bifurcation while its Ingram input still needs early McMullen rigidity. Fresh assembly has 2,956 stages and 8,563 edges and is acyclic; neither proposed Part II is a live vertex.

Confirmed that E7's assertion that (3.2) remains proved is unsupported. Published p.10 and arXiv v3 p.15 invoke DM1 Proposition 4.8 from the diagonal point. DM1 v2 p.19, section 4.3, explicitly requires an isolated intersection with the continued repelling section. Re-derivation: the first landing germ has dimension k-r-1; whenever z in that germ and y0 lie on a common family member, (z,y0,...,y0) is another simultaneous landing point. A positive-dimensional such germ defeats isolatedness. The affine-line incidence model in dimension three illustrates this mechanism with r=1, ell=4, k=3. However dimension of M_d^cm alone does not prove the claimed global generically finite A3 parameterization, nor all the global hypotheses of that example. GOV Lemma 6.8 proves nonzero top bifurcation mass off the flexible locus, not the missing isolatedness. Fix E7, item 27 and the brief to record both nonvanishing and the witness as unclosed inputs of Proposition 3.1/Theorem 1.8. Supply a valid construction or another proof; do not assert the theorem or measure is false, or prescribe the unproved global example/off-diagonal recipe as an established repair.

Route item 11 to an explicitly committed AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry Part II design, importing the retained projective/Hilbert foundations, and update the height/bifurcation consumers. Define the open locus for closures of irreducible subvarieties meeting Y, the bounded-degree finite union, incidence and field-of-definition interfaces precisely; do not conflate it with the Chow lemma or promise an unchanged R09 blueprint will supply it.

Preserve arithmetic descent and field hypotheses.

Confirmed that 'the marked critical point lies in the basin at such parabolic parameters' is too broad: a parabolic basin contains some critical point, not necessarily the selected c. Published p.13 and item 28 need a c-specific existence/density statement in the local one-dimensional slice used by Proposition 3.2. MSS density alone does not identify that critical point. Correct the universal statement and retain the exact selected-c lemma as a named input/gap until an appropriate proof is supplied. I do not certify the red team's Montel-periodic-to-parabolic recipe: Dujardin's introduction and GOV's proof use prerepelling approximation, and that by itself does not establish this stronger basin conclusion. Any replacement proof must show the same c remains in the basin and that the cycle is nonpersistent.
